headline: DU student tears up Jinnah's photographs at Ducsu archive
summary: A student and activists from the Students' Federation of Bangladesh destroyed images of Pakistan's founder in protest over the archive's content.
details: A fourth-year Urdu Department student, Muhammad Abu Tayab, smashed a frame and tore up photographs of Muhammad Ali Jinnah at the Ducsu archive this afternoon.
The act was supported by leaders and activists of the Students' Federation of Bangladesh's Dhaka University unit, who also provided a Dawn newspaper clipping of Jinnah for Tayab to destroy.
Tayab questioned why a 'villain' like Jinnah should be displayed, citing the history of the 1971 Liberation War and the Language Movement.
In place of the destroyed images, the federation displayed a photograph of convicted war criminal Ghulam Azam being beaten with shoes in 1981.
Ducsu General Secretary SM Farhad defended the original display, stating Jinnah's stance against the Bengali language was shown to highlight history, not to honor him.
The archive had reopened on Sunday with images depicting events between 1905 and 1971, though critics noted the absence of a prominent photograph of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman.
The Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal had previously condemned the display of Jinnah's photos and the proposed renaming of Madhur Canteen as 'Ishrat Manzil'.
caption:
A student smashed frames and tore up photos of Muhammad Ali Jinnah at the Ducsu archive in protest.

A fourth-year Urdu Department student, Muhammad Abu Tayab, smashed a frame and tore up photographs of Muhammad Ali Jinnah at the Ducsu archive this afternoon.

The act was supported by leaders and activists of the Students' Federation of Bangladesh's Dhaka University unit, who also provided a Dawn newspaper clipping of Jinnah for Tayab to destroy.

Tayab questioned why a 'villain' like Jinnah should be displayed, citing the history of the 1971 Liberation War and the Language Movement.

In place of the destroyed images, the federation displayed a photograph of convicted war criminal Ghulam Azam being beaten with shoes in 1981.

Ducsu General Secretary SM Farhad defended the original display, stating Jinnah's stance against the Bengali language was shown to highlight history, not to honor him.

The archive had reopened on Sunday with images depicting events between 1905 and 1971, though critics noted the absence of a prominent photograph of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman.

The Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal had previously condemned the display of Jinnah's photos and the proposed renaming of Madhur Canteen as 'Ishrat Manzil'.

headline_marked: Industrial [[gas supply to return to near previous levels]] by tomorrow evening: PM
headline: Industrial gas supply to return to near previous levels by tomorrow evening: PM
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman assured business leaders that technical issues at an LNG terminal have been resolved, promising a return to stable energy supplies.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman announced that gas supply to industries and factories will return to near its previous levels by tomorrow evening. This follows the resolution of a technical problem caused by an accident at one of Bangladesh's two floating LNG terminals.

During a three-hour exchange with business leaders and media professionals at the Secretariat in Dhaka, the Prime Minister emphasized that energy problems are inherited and cannot be solved instantly.

The government has identified the core issues and established timelines for implementation. To further secure energy needs, preparations are largely complete to set up a third floating LNG terminal under a government-to-government arrangement.

The third terminal is expected to be connected to the gas supply system by December 2027. The Prime Minister noted that uninterrupted energy supplies are essential for Bangladesh to reach its goal of a $1 trillion economy by 2034.

Tarique Rahman urged cooperation from businesses and the media, warning that instability could disrupt trade and the wider economy. He stated that the government has openly acknowledged the problems and is working to address them.
The meeting was attended by high-level officials including the Commerce Minister, Finance and Planning Adviser, and leaders from FBCCI, BGMEA, and BKMEA.
